title: Z.AI / generic collector contract
description:
The wire contract a site-local collector for Claude Code with Z.AI (plan §7.3), or any other generic/non-native provider, must emit. This is deliberately NOT a distinct format: subgov has exactly one normalized quota contract (§6), and a Z.AI collector is held to it verbatim -- 'Apply exactly the same freshness and window validation as native sources.' This file exists as a stable, standalone entry point so a third-party collector author can build against a contract without reading Rust source (src/model.rs, src/source.rs); it re-exports schema/quota-snapshot.schema.json by reference rather than copying it, so the two can never drift apart. See that file for the full property-by-property documentation.

Transport (§7.4, reused verbatim -- no Z.AI-specific transport exists): emit this document one of three ways, chosen in the account's `source` config:
- `command`: an argv array (never interpreted by a shell) whose stdout is exactly one JSON document matching this schema; diagnostics go to stderr, not stdout.
- `normalized_file`: a file at a configured path, replaced with an atomic (rename-into-place) write so subgov never observes a torn read.
- `normalized_http`: a GET against a loopback or otherwise access-controlled URL. Redirects must be disabled or same-origin-only; there is no automatic credential injection.

Security boundary: provider credentials for the underlying account (Z.AI or otherwise) belong entirely to the site-local collector process. They must never appear in subgov's own configuration, command-line arguments, or environment as passed by subgov -- subgov's `command` source only ever sees the collector's argv, never a secret. subgov will not add arbitrary secret headers to a `normalized_http` request in v1; put any credential the collector process itself needs into its own environment or config, not into anything subgov passes to it.

A working example of a `command` collector account is examples/claude-zai.yaml; examples/data/claude-zai.json is a valid instance of the emitted document.
